# Provision Vault identities with SCIM

@include 'alerts/enterprise-only.mdx'

@include 'alerts/beta.mdx'

Vault Enterprise supports System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM)
2.0 as a beta feature for provisioning identity users and groups from external
identity platforms.

Vault exposes SCIM through the identity secrets engine.

- SCIM users map to Vault
  [entities](/vault/docs/concepts/identity#entities-and-aliases).
- When you configure `alias_mount_accessor`, SCIM users also create
  mount-bound [entity aliases](/vault/docs/concepts/identity#mount-bound-aliases).
- SCIM groups map to Vault
  [internal identity groups](/vault/docs/concepts/identity#external-vs-internal-groups).
- A SCIM client can manage only the users and groups it owns.
- SCIM does not manage Vault policies.

The SCIM interface is a thin wrapper over the standard Vault identity APIs. SCIM
requests use the same request serialization and write to the same identity
store as other identity requests. Configure rate limits for the SCIM client and
its identity provider (IdP) so a provisioning burst cannot overload the
identity store.

## Before you start

- You must have Vault Enterprise 2.x.x or later.
- You must have permissions to enable auth methods and manage identity resources.
- You should know the auth method you want to use for the SCIM client.

Any Vault auth method can work for SCIM if authentication resolves to the Vault
entity configured as the access grant principal (`access_grant_principal`) for the SCIM client.

Some SCIM clients only support a static bearer token. In those cases, token
auth usually gives you the simplest setup because you can mint a token tied to
an entity alias and pass that token directly to the connector.

## SCIM endpoints and namespaces

Vault exposes SCIM endpoints under the following endpoints:

- `/v1/identity/scim/v2`: SCIM base path for `/Users`, `/Groups`, `/ServiceProviderConfig`, `/Schemas` and `/ResourceTypes`.
- `/v1/identity/scim/client` (and `/clients`): management of Vault SCIM clients.

If you use Vault Enterprise namespaces, you can address SCIM in either of these
ways:

- Put the namespace in the request path, such as
  `/v1/admin/identity/scim/v2/Users`.
- Use the standard Vault namespace header with the non-namespaced path.

## Configure a SCIM client

Create a SCIM client before you send SCIM protocol requests.

Each SCIM client represents one external provisioning system. The SCIM client
configuration consists of these fields:

- `client_name` (part of the URL): Namespace-scoped name for the external system.
- `access_grant_principal`: ID of the Vault entity that authorizes SCIM API
  requests for that client.
- `alias_mount_accessor`: Optional auth mount accessor. When set, Vault also
  creates a mount-bound entity alias for each SCIM user.
- `default_schema_version`: Optional Vault extension schema version. New
  clients default to `2.2`. Set this to `2.0` to keep using the original
  extension for backward compatibility. Clients created before this option was
  introduced continue to use `2.0`.
- `allow_user_adoption` and `allow_group_adoption`: Optional flags that allow
  the client to adopt eligible existing entities and groups. Both default to
  `false`.
- `max_active_tokens` and `max_token_ttl`: Limits for
  [`scim` tokens](#scim-token-type). `max_active_tokens` defaults to `2`, and
  `max_token_ttl` of `0` uses the cluster default.

Vault enforces these rules:

- `access_grant_principal` must refer to an existing entity in the same
  namespace.
- `alias_mount_accessor`, when set, must refer to an existing non-local auth
  mount in the same namespace.
- `alias_mount_accessor` is immutable after creation.
- A SCIM client can only manage the users and groups it created.

Vault limits `alias_mount_accessor` to non-local auth mounts.

## Extension schemas and compatibility

Vault supports the following Vault-specific SCIM extension schemas:

| Resource | Schema | Attributes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| User | `urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:vault:2.2:User` | `entityName`, `aliases`, and `metadata` |
| Group | `urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:vault:2.2:Group` | `metadata` |
| User (deprecated) | `urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:vault:2.0:Metadata` | `items` metadata array |

The 2.2 schemas evolve additively. Vault introduces another schema version only
when it must make an incompatible change to an existing attribute.

The deprecated 2.0 metadata schema remains supported so existing connectors
that were built against it keep working. Do not include it with the 2.2 User
extension in the same request. When a request includes either extension
block, its schema URI must also be present in the request's `schemas` array.
Vault rejects undeclared extension blocks and requests that include both User
extensions.

Each SCIM client determines its own extension schema version through
`default_schema_version`, so different clients in the same namespace can use
different versions. Vault uses that client's version for every request it makes,
unless the request declares an extension schema itself.

When you omit `default_schema_version`, newly created clients return 2.2
extensions and clients created before this setting return 2.0 metadata for
backward compatibility. Set the client default to `2.0` if a connector still
depends on the original extension.

The 2.2 User extension supports the following behavior:

- `entityName` lets a client with `alias_mount_accessor` keep the entity name
  separate from `userName`. Without a primary alias mount, Vault requires the
  entity name to match `userName`.
- `aliases` manages secondary entity aliases. Each entry includes
  `mount_accessor` and `name`. An omitted array preserves managed secondary
  aliases; an empty array removes them. Vault never removes unmanaged aliases.
- `metadata` maps key/value pairs to entity metadata. An omitted value on
  update preserves metadata; an empty array clears it.

The 2.2 Group extension maps `metadata` to group metadata. An omitted
metadata value preserves metadata and an empty array clears it.

## Authentication model

A SCIM client authenticates to Vault through a supported auth method, gets
a Vault token, and uses that token for SCIM requests. Vault infers the SCIM
client identity based on the token entity.

At a high level:

1. Create a Vault entity to represent the SCIM client.
1. Bind the entity to a SCIM client with `access_grant_principal`.
1. Authenticate through an auth method that resolves to that entity.
1. Use the resulting Vault token for SCIM API calls.

Vault rejects SCIM requests if the token does not resolve to the configured entity or the entity does not have an associated SCIM client.

## Simple bearer-token setup

The following example uses the token auth method because it is easy to connect
to SCIM products that expect a static bearer token. But you can use any auth
method that maps back to the configured entity for the SCIM client.

### 1. Create a policy for the SCIM client token

```shell-session
$ vault policy write scim-client - <<'EOF'
path "identity/scim/v2/*" {
  capabilities = ["create", "read", "update", "delete", "list"]
}
EOF
```

### 2. Create the Vault entity for the SCIM client

```shell-session
$ vault write -format=json identity/entity name="scim-client"
```

Save the returned entity ID.

### 3. Create the SCIM client configuration

```shell-session
$ vault write identity/scim/client/example-client \
    access_grant_principal="<entity_id>"
```

If you want Vault to create aliases for provisioned users as well, include the
`alias_mount_accessor` parameter. For example:


### 4. Create an entity alias on the token auth mount

List auth mounts and record the accessor for `token/`.

```shell-session
$ vault auth list
```

Create an alias on that mount for the SCIM client entity.

```shell-session
$ vault write identity/entity-alias \
    name="example-client" \
    mount_accessor="<token_mount_accessor>" \
    canonical_id="<entity_id>"
```

### 5. Create a token role and mint a bearer token

```shell-session
$ vault write auth/token/roles/example-scim \
    allowed_entity_aliases="example-client" \
    orphan=true \
    token_no_default_policy=true

$ vault token create \
    -role=example-scim \
    -entity-alias=example-client \
    -policy=scim-client \
    -type=scim \
    -orphan \
    -no-default-policy
```

Use the returned token value as the bearer token for SCIM requests.

We strongly recommend planning token renewal or rotation around the TTL configured on
your token auth mount.

### SCIM token type

Use `token_type=scim` when you issue a static token for a SCIM client. A SCIM
token is associated with the entity that represents the client and Vault limits
it using that client's `max_active_tokens` and `max_token_ttl` settings.

SCIM tokens must be non-renewable orphan tokens. Vault rejects an issuance
request when the effective entity is not a SCIM client's
`access_grant_principal`, the requested TTL exceeds `max_token_ttl`, or the
client has reached its active-token limit. Revoke an existing token before you
issue another token when the limit is reached.

Vault restricts a SCIM token to a fixed set of paths: the SCIM protocol
endpoints under `identity/scim/v2`, and its own
`auth/token/lookup-self`, `auth/token/renew-self`, `auth/token/revoke-self`,
and `sys/capabilities-self`. Vault rejects requests to any other path with
that token, so you cannot use a SCIM token for general Vault API calls.

## Send SCIM requests

Use the Vault token in the request header to call the SCIM endpoint:

```shell-session
$ curl \
    --header "X-Vault-Token: ${VAULT_TOKEN}" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/scim+json" \
    ${VAULT_ADDR}/v1/identity/scim/v2/ServiceProviderConfig
```


## How Vault maps SCIM resources

| SCIM resource | Vault resource | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `User` | Entity | `userName` maps to the entity name and `externalId` maps to the entity external ID. |
| `Group` | Internal identity group | `displayName` maps to the group name. |

Important behavior:

- `externalId` is optional when you create a SCIM user.
- `externalId` stays fixed after creation and does not need to be unique within a namespace.
- Group members must reference Vault user resource IDs.
- A SCIM client can only add the users it owns to a group.

If the SCIM client sets `alias_mount_accessor`, Vault creates a mount-bound
entity alias for each provisioned user and keeps the alias name aligned with
the SCIM `userName`.

## Adopt, link, and unlink resources

Use adoption and linking only when you need to bring existing Vault identity
resources under SCIM management.

- To adopt an entity through `POST /Users`, set `allow_user_adoption=true` on
  the client. Vault can adopt an unmanaged entity when `userName` matches an
  existing login alias.
- To adopt a group through SCIM, set `allow_group_adoption=true` and use a
  `PUT` or `PATCH` request for an eligible unmanaged group. `POST` creates a
  new group and does not adopt an existing group.
- Use the administrative `link-entity` or `link-group` endpoints to associate
  an existing unmanaged entity or group with a SCIM client. All members of a
  linked group must already belong to that client.
- Use `unlink-entity` or `unlink-group` to remove a client's ownership without
  deleting the resource. Unlinking an entity clears its `externalId` and can
  require confirmation to make secondary aliases unmanaged or remove group
  memberships.

When `allow_group_adoption` is `true`, a SCIM client can see unmanaged groups.
Vault filters each group's members to users owned by the requesting client. The
client can adopt an eligible group with `PUT` or `PATCH`.

After you link or adopt a resource, the owning SCIM client controls its
SCIM-managed fields. You cannot move a managed resource to a different SCIM
client. Vault also rejects identity-entity merge requests that involve
SCIM-managed entities.

## Supported protocol surface

Vault supports these SCIM areas:

- SCIM client configuration through `/identity/scim/client`
- User create, read, list, replace, patch, and delete
- Group create, read, list, replace, patch, and delete
- Discovery endpoints for `Schemas`, `ResourceTypes`, and
  `ServiceProviderConfig`

Vault returns SCIM responses as `application/scim+json`.

## Current limitations

- Vault does not support `/Me`.
- Vault does not support SCIM bulk operations.
- Vault does not support sort, ETag, or change password operations.
- User `PATCH` only supports a single `replace` operation for `active`.
- Group `PATCH` only supports member add and remove operations.
- Vault supports limited filtering on list endpoints.
  - `/Users` supports `eq` for `userName`, `externalId`, and `active`.
  - `/Users` and `/Groups` support `gt`, `ge`, `lt`, and `le` for
    `meta.lastModified`.
  - `/Groups` supports `eq` for `displayName`.
- Vault does not support arbitrary SCIM filter expressions beyond those
  documented fields and operators.
- Group members must use Vault user resource IDs, not `userName` or
  `externalId`.
- `externalId` is optional when you create a user. If provided, you cannot
  update it later through SCIM or normal identity API writes while the entity
  is SCIM-managed. Multiple users may share the same `externalId` value.
- User `groups` only shows direct memberships in groups managed by the same SCIM
  client.
- `alias_mount_accessor` is immutable after client creation and remains tied to
  the auth mount strategy you choose for that client.

## Deleting a SCIM client

Deleting a SCIM client with managed resources requires an explicit cleanup
strategy. This requirement is a breaking change from the initial beta
behavior, which deleted linked resources automatically.

Use `delete-linked-resources=true` to delete the owned entities, aliases, and
groups, or use `unlink-resources=true` to preserve them and remove their SCIM
association. These options are mutually exclusive. Include the option as an
explicit query string when you call the HTTP API:

```shell-session
$ curl \
    --request DELETE \
    --header "X-Vault-Token: ${VAULT_TOKEN}" \
    "${VAULT_ADDR}/v1/identity/scim/client/example-client?unlink-resources=true"
```

Vault blocks new requests for the client and completes the selected cleanup in
the background. Review the resources owned by a client before you choose a
strategy.

## Migrate from the initial beta

When you upgrade an existing beta deployment:

1. Update SCIM clients that use the deprecated metadata extension to declare
   `urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:vault:2.0:Metadata` in every
   request that includes its extension block. Migrate to the 2.2 User
   extension when your IdP supports it.
1. Do not send the 2.0 metadata and 2.2 User extension schemas together.
1. Review every client-deletion automation. Add exactly one of
   `delete-linked-resources=true` or `unlink-resources=true` when the client
   owns resources.
1. Review SCIM client names for case-only duplicates. Vault treats client names
   as case-insensitive.
1. Configure `default_schema_version` explicitly when a connector requires a
   stable response schema.
1. Stop using `identity/entity/merge` for SCIM-managed entities. Vault rejects
   those requests to preserve SCIM ownership boundaries.
